newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Editorials - Aug 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Editorials - Aug 1.

text.p: These are highlights of comments in the Hong Kong press. The views expressed are those of the newspapers quoted and do not represent an editorial viewpoint of Reuters.

-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL said that after the handover, few Hong Kong people had any nationalistic feelings, while most people treasured the old system and lifestyle, and hoped that they could remain intact. After taking office, Chief Executive Tung Chee-hwa has not talked much about the prospect of Hong Kong's democratic development. The paper said that if Hong Kong could develop a sound democratic system to let different political interests voice their opininns, it would contribute a lot more to China's modernisation than it had done in the past 20 years.

-- The Beijing-funded TA KUNG PAO said the Special Administrative Region government's first month of operation was a "fantastic beginning". It said Chief Executive Tung had kept his promises and demonstrated a steady working style. Taiwanese would change their opinion on the "one country, two systems" concept, if they watched developments in Hong Kong, it said.

-- The English-language SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST said it hoped China's Foreign Ministry could become more adventurous, perhaps using its Hong Kong office as a bridge for contacts with some groups, which would be difficult to conduct in the more formalistic atmosphere of Beijing. It said the ministry should also take a more flexible attitude towards Hong Kong's external affairs.
